rappel_detail.pull: 60 m is the stated minimum rope for this line; a 70 m makes every station comfortable.
rappel_detail.notes: First rappel, off a tree down a short 5.0 slab from the summit exit area.
rappel_detail.anchor: tree, on the 5.0 slab, about 30m below and skier's-right of the summit exit
rappel_detail.station: The descent does not start where the route tops out. The rappel line begins roughly 30 m down and skier's right of the top-out, reached by walking and downclimbing from the summit exit, so hunt for it rather than rigging off the first thing at the finish.

rappel_detail.notes: First of four bolted single-rope rappels with a 60m rope.
rappel_detail.anchor: bolted station (blank section of West Face)
hazards: hanging station - get tethered in before unweighting the rope
rappel_detail.station: Top of the bolted line down the right side of the West Face. The first rappel drops straight down the face to a station described as a hanging belay with no ledge to stand on.

rappel_detail.notes: Continues down the bolted West Face line.
hazards: the line steps sideways here, so the next anchor is not directly below the rope
rappel_detail.station: Next bolted station down the face; from here the line is described as trending climber's left rather than falling straight down.

rappel_detail.pull: A 70 m rope removes the squeeze entirely.
rappel_detail.notes: Continues down the bolted West Face line.
hazards: rope ends land in the working zone on a 60 m - knot both ends
mixed piton-and-bolt anchor at one station on this line; inspect before loading
rappel_detail.station: Commonly reported as the third rappel of the bolted sequence, and the tight one: on a 60 m rope parties describe reaching down to clip a tether to the anchor and then feeding rope through the device to close the last bit. One station on this line is described as a piton backed by a bolt rather than two bolts.

rappel_detail.pull: Pulls on this line are reported clean and direct, but at least one rappel clears a roof, so expect the ends to hang free of the wall.
rappel_detail.notes: Final bolted rappel reaching the base.
rappel_detail.station: Lowest station; the line puts you back essentially where packs are left at the base. Accounts differ on the bottom of the sequence - some describe the last one or two rappels off tree slings above and below the chimney rather than off bolts.

set.rappels: Rappel the Chockstone Route line on a 60 m rope: one tree rappel, then four bolted West Face stations. Or the full bolted West Face line from its top, six rappels on a 70 m rope.
set.rappel_count_note: This is the current recommended descent (a tree rap near the top followed by four bolted West Face stations). An older/original variant instead makes 5 rappels straight down the ascent gully - including one free-hanging rappel off the chockstone - through loose, windy terrain, and is less commonly used now that the bolted line exists. Individual rappel lengths are not published; every station is reached on a single 60 m rope.
